title: Model list is empty in mesh-node scenes: list the repo's own DSL graphs (fixtures included) without the never-built staging directory
description:
User report 2026-10-03: in the mesh-node viewer family of scenes (ring-tool, ring-regions, mesh viewer) the model list is empty and the [ / ] model keys do nothing. Cause: MeshNodeViewerScene builds its catalog with ModelCatalog.staging(ModelCatalog.stagingRoot()), which only scans ~/.ix/ixdar-models (or $IXDAR_MODEL_DIR). That directory is meant to be filled by a sync-models tool (VIEW-6, planned for the Daud repo) that was never built, so on this machine it does not exist and the list is empty. The DSL graphs the user actually edits, such as dsl/fixtures/fertility_rings.dsl, are never offered.

Make the model list work without the staging directory. The catalog always includes the repo's own DSL graphs: every .dsl under ixdar-app/src/main/resources/dsl/, recursively, fixtures/ included, loaded as DSL resources (the -Dixdar.mesh.dsl path), so Ctrl+S in the ring tool writes the tracked file just as a launch with -Dixdar.mesh.dsl does. Merge in the staging directory's entries when it exists, de-duplicating graphs it symlinks from the repo. Group or prefix the names so repo graphs and staged files are distinguishable, and keep the order stable so [ and ] step predictably. [ / ] and the model menu both work in every scene built on MeshNodeViewerScene. Record on VIEW-6 that the scenes no longer depend on it for the repo's own graphs.

Rework 2026-10-03 (user review): the model menu shows every model at once in a scrollable list instead of a 15-row window, with no '... N more above ([ steps back)' or '... N more below (] steps on)' lines. Scrolling the mouse wheel over the list scrolls the list and does not orbit or zoom the camera; outside the list the wheel keeps its camera behaviour. Reference: Ixdar's main knot view (MainScene) already does this with MouseTrap.subscribeScrollRegion and InfoPane's scrollOffsetY with drawHyperStringRows; the 3D scenes route the wheel through OrbitMouseTrap, so the list region has to win there too. Recompute and Controls stay reachable (below the list or in their own region).

Rework 2, 2026-10-03 (user review of the scrolling menu):
a. Two scroll boxes: one for the model list and one for the controls, each scrolling on its own.
b. The MODELS and CONTROLS titles sit above their boxes and do not scroll.
c. Reverse the wheel direction (it scrolls the wrong way today).
d. When the menu opens, the current .dsl is centred in the model box.
e. Bug: with the cursor over the left part of the menu text the wheel still orbits/zooms the camera. The scroll region apparently does not cover each box's full drawn area (likely a bounds or coordinate-space mismatch between the registered region and where the text is drawn, or the strip's x origin). Each box's whole rectangle must take the wheel.

Rework 3, 2026-10-03: control-hint and model rows that are wider than the menu strip are cut off at the edge (seen on the editing scene's long tool-switch hint). Wrap long rows onto continuation lines inside their box instead, with scroll limits, centring and click hit areas counting wrapped rows correctly. Also the first row of the models box is drawn half under the fixed MODELS title; the box's clip should start below the title.

Rework 4, 2026-10-03 (user review of the code):
f. MouseTrap must not know about its OrbitMouseTrap child. Done by the coordinator: ScrollHandler.takesWheelFromOrbit and scrollHandlerUnderCursor(boolean orbitTakersOnly) are gone; MouseTrap.scrollHandlerUnderCursor(Predicate<ScrollHandler>) is generic, and the opt-in lives in OrbitMouseTrap.WheelClaimer (claimsWheel) with OrbitMouseTrap.wheelClaimerUnderCursor(); SceneModelMenu and MenuScrollBox implement WheelClaimer.
g. No duplicated wrapping: HyperString already wraps (the wrap flag, setLineOffsetFromTopRow breaking at the word that would cross the camera width, per-word click bounds, returning rows used) and Font.drawHyperStringRows draws it. MenuScrollBox's own wrapRow and its parallel line/row/click arrays must go; the box builds its rows as a HyperString (one line per row, the row's click on its words) and lets HyperString lay out, wrap, hit-test and count rows. Extend HyperString only where it lacks something the menu needs (for example a public way to enable wrapping, or a hard break for a token wider than the box), not with a second wrapper.

h. MeshNodeViewerScene must not know about the file system (user, 2026-10-03). Today it resolves the repo dsl root (src/main/resources/dsl, falling back to MeshLoader.MODULE_DIRECTORY; added by this ticket), turns -Dixdar.model into a choice by probing directories and files (requestedModel), maps a resource name to its tracked file (dslResourceFile, the working path for saves), reads graph text with Files (loadDslSource and the DSL load path) and opens collections by Path. Move that knowledge into ModelChoice (a choice knows where it lives, how to read its source and where a save writes) and ModelCatalog (finding the repo dsl root, resolving a launch property to a choice); the scene asks the choice and never touches Files or Path. Keep the web build working (no java.nio.file at runtime there; it reads packaged resources).
definition-of-done:
1. With no ~/.ix/ixdar-models, the ring-tool scene's model list shows every .dsl under resources/dsl/ including fixtures/fertility_rings.dsl, and [ / ] step through them. 2. Loading fixtures/fertility_rings.dsl from the list and pressing Ctrl+S in the ring tool writes the tracked file (tested on a temporary copy of the resource tree, never the user's fixture). 3. With a staging directory present, its entries appear too, without duplicates. 4. Screenshot of the populated list in tmp/. 5. Build checkstyle-green.

6. All repo graphs are reachable in the menu by wheel-scrolling over the list; the camera does not move while doing so (orbit state before and after); no [ / ] hint lines remain in the list; screenshots at the top and the bottom of the list.

7. Two independently scrolling boxes with fixed titles; wheel direction reversed; the launched .dsl centred on open; the wheel over any point of either box, the left edge of the text included, scrolls that box and leaves the camera unchanged (orbit state checked at several x positions across each box).

8. A hint longer than the strip wraps onto a second line within the controls box (screenshot), scrolling and clicks still land on the right rows, and no row is drawn under a fixed title.

9. MenuScrollBox has no wrapping code of its own and keeps no line-to-row arrays; wrapping, click hit areas and row counts come from HyperString; DoD 7 and 8 behaviour unchanged (screenshots, unit tests adapted).

10. MeshNodeViewerScene imports neither java.nio.file nor java.io.File and has no path probing; ModelChoice/ModelCatalog own resolving, reading and the save target; loading, saving (Ctrl+S to the tracked file, tested on a copy) and the launch properties behave as before; web build OK.
testing-plan: 1. Unit test: catalog over a temp resource tree with nested folders, with and without a staging dir. 2. F5 the ring-tool scene, open the model list, step with [ and ].
changes-made: ModelCatalog.repoGraphsAndStaging(repoDslRoot, stagingRoot) builds the mesh-node model list: every .dsl under ixdar-app/src/main/resources/dsl/ recursively (fixtures included), named 'repo: <relative path>' and sorted, then the staging directory's entries (when it exists) prefixed 'staged ' ('staged DSL: x', 'staged OBJ voyage: x', 'staged glTF: x'), dropping staged files whose real path is a repo graph. Repo graphs load by absolute path of the tracked file, so Ctrl+S writes the tracked file. MeshNodeViewerScene.createCatalog uses it and puts the cursor on the launched graph (-Dixdar.mesh.dsl), so [ / ] step from there and the menu highlights it. SceneModelMenu shows a 15-row window of the model list centred on the current model with '... N more above/below' lines, so the 38+ entries no longer push Recompute and Controls off screen. The display separator changed from a bullet (missing from the font) to ': '. Fixed a pre-existing web-build break: loadDslSource used Files.readString (TeaVM lacks it); now readAllBytes + UTF-8.

Verification: new unit test unit.model.ModelCatalogTest (nested temp resource tree with and without a staging dir, symlink de-dup, [ / ] wrap) green; full mvn test 348 run, 0 failures; mvn -q compile checkstyle-clean; tools/teavm-build.sh OK (classes.js 7.8 MB, 0 errors). With no ~/.ix/ixdar-models the ring-tool lists 38 repo graphs (fixtures/fertility_rings.dsl included), cursor on repo: skull.dsl [32/38]; ] / [ stepped and wrapped (40/40 -> 1/40 -> 40/40) through the /input key route. Ctrl+S tested on a throwaway copy fixtures/view12_rings_copy.dsl picked via the model route: R, click, Enter, Ctrl+S logged 'saved 1 ring(s) to .../src/main/resources/dsl/fixtures/view12_rings_copy.dsl'; the copy was deleted afterwards and fertility_rings.dsl's sha256 and git diff are unchanged. With IXDAR_MODEL_DIR=tmp/staging (a symlink to fertility_rings.dsl, a staged .dsl and a glTF) the list had 40 entries: the symlink de-duplicated, staged entries after the repo graphs. Web: no folder to walk, so the list is empty and shows '(no models found)'; [ / ] are no-ops. Screenshots: tmp/view12-model-list.png, tmp/view12-model-list-after-right-brackets.png, tmp/view12-model-list-after-left-brackets.png, tmp/view-12-launch.png. Known: repo: test_bridge.dsl fails to execute (halfEdgeEdge null), a graph problem unrelated to the list.

Rework 2026-10-03: the ESC model menu lists every model again (the 15-row window and the '... N more above/below' [ / ] hint lines are gone) and scrolls with the wheel, following MainScene/InfoPane: SceneModelMenu implements MouseTrap.ScrollHandler, keeps scrollOffsetY (clamped to [0, maximumScrollOffsetY] measured from the last row at draw) and draws with drawHyperStringRows; ModelScene.initPanes subscribes the menu strip with MouseTrap.subscribeScrollRegion. OrbitMouseTrap.paintUpdate now hands pending wheel ticks to a subscribed region under the cursor whose handler returns ScrollHandler.takesWheelFromOrbit() (the menu, only while open) before zooming; the default is false, so the terminal strip's existing subscription still zooms in 3D scenes. MouseTrap's region hit test moved into scrollHandlerUnderCursor(boolean), shared by both traps. Recompute and Controls are reached by scrolling to the bottom.

Rework verification: ring-tool, menu open, cursor over the list: orbit before {azimuth 0.785, elevation 0.419, distance 3.596} and after 10 wheel events down and 10 up identical; scrolled down to the end (all 38 repo graphs, Recompute and every Controls row reachable), back up to a pixel-identical top (image-diff rmse 0). Cursor over the mesh: wheel zooms (distance 3.596 -> 2.495). Menu closed over the same strip: wheel zooms. Menu open over its bottom corner (overlapping the terminal strip): menu scrolls, camera still. mvn test 348/0 failures, compile checkstyle-clean, teavm-build OK, ixd wt done passed. Screenshots: tmp/view12-menu-top.png, tmp/view12-menu-scrolled.png (bottom), tmp/view12-menu-back-to-top.png; orbit dumps tmp/orbit-before.json, tmp/orbit-after-down.json.

Rework 2: the ESC menu is a fixed MODELS title over a models box, then fixed Recompute and CONTROLS rows over a controls box. Each box is a new MenuScrollBox (gui/ui/menu): framebuffer Bounds that are its viewport (rows clip and clicks are bounded to it), its own scrollOffsetY clamped from the row count, subscribed as its own MouseTrap scroll region (ModelScene.initPanes subscribes models box, controls box, then the whole strip, which swallows the wheel over the titles). SceneModelMenu.layout puts the controls box at the bottom, as tall as its rows up to 40% of the strip, and gives the models box the rest. Wheel direction reversed (negative ticks, the wheel rolled toward you, move on to later rows). Opening the menu centres the current model row in the models box. Cause of the left-of-text bug: MouseTrap.scrollHandlerUnderCursor compared the raw cursor in window pixels (lastX, windowHeight - lastY) with Bounds that are framebuffer viewports; on this 1.25-scale display the framebuffer is 1.25x the window, so the region started at window x = fbWidth - 420 while the strip is drawn from (fbWidth - 420) / 1.25, and only the strip's right ~45 window px took the wheel. It now tests normalizedPosX/Y (framebuffer pixels, y up), the coordinates the HyperString click test already used, and returns null before the first cursor move. ui-state reports each open box as a scene_menu_box text element with scrollOffsetY, maximumScrollOffsetY and its rectangle.

Rework 2 verification: unit.input.ScrollRegionHitTest (window 800x600, framebuffer 1000x750): window x 465/630/799 over a strip whose framebuffer left is 580 reach its handler (the old test failed for x < 580), x 463 does not, and a bottom box is hit y-up in framebuffer pixels. Full mvn test 352 run, 0 failures; mvn -q compile checkstyle-clean; teavm-build OK (0 errors). ring-tool (headless 1024x1024, launched with fixtures/fertility_rings.dsl): on open the models box (fb y 450-994, centre 722) has the current row at y 707-737 (centre 722), offset 103 of 596; reopening re-centres. Wheel at x = 605 (left edge of the text), 610, 700, 850, 1020 over each box: that box's offset moved (models 596 -> 498 -> 401 -> 304 -> 206 -> 108 on wheel up; controls 300 -> 202 -> 105 -> 7 -> 0), the other box unchanged, orbit {az 0.7854, el 0.4189, d 268.5152} identical before and after every event; over the MODELS and CONTROLS titles nothing moves. Wheel toward you scrolls on to later rows. Outside the menu with it open the wheel zooms (d 268.5 -> 387.0); menu closed over the strip it zooms (387.0 -> 537.0 -> 372.6); over the terminal strip with the menu closed it zooms as on master (the orbit trap never hands the wheel to the terminal; terminal scrollOffsetY stays 0). Clicking the current row in the scrolled box reloads it. Screenshots: tmp/view12-r2-menu-opened.png (current dsl centred), tmp/view12-r2-models-scrolled.png, tmp/view12-r2-controls-scrolled.png, tmp/view12-r2-both-at-end.png, tmp/view12-r2-both-at-top.png; probe output tmp/v12-probe-boxes.txt, tmp/v12-probe-boxes-up.txt, tmp/v12-probe-rest.txt.

Rework 3 (2026-10-03): MenuScrollBox now holds rows (text, colour, click) and wraps each to the box width at the last space that fits, hard-breaking an unbroken token; every wrapped line carries its row's click, and the scroll limit, centring of the current model (middle of its wrapped lines) and controls-box height all count wrapped lines. SceneCollectionMenu rows go through the same box, so long manifest paths wrap too. Boxes are laid out whole lines tall with the models box directly under MODELS, and lines are drawn at whole-line scroll offsets, so no row is ever cut or drawn under a fixed title. Verified: MenuScrollBoxWrapTest (6 tests: break at space, hard break, line-to-row click mapping, scroll limit and centring with wrapped rows, whole-line draw offset); mvn test 358/358 green; mvn -q compile (checkstyle) clean; teavm-build OK; ring-tool run with a staged DSL whose 70-char name wraps onto three lines: a click on the third line loaded it and highlighted all three (tmp/view12-r3-wrapped-model-row.png, tmp/view12-r3-wrapped-model-row-clicked.png); partial wheel scroll leaves the first models row whole under the title (tmp/view12-r3-models-top-mid-scroll.png, tmp/view12-r3-models-top-on-open.png); wheel over the left edge of both boxes still scrolls them and leaves the orbit unchanged. No control hint in this tree is wider than the strip (the long tool-switch hint is CRAW-32's), so no screenshot of a wrapped hint; hints use the same wrapping path as model rows.

Rework 4 g (2026-10-03): MenuScrollBox (259 -> 165 lines) no longer wraps anything itself. wrapRow, wrapRows, textWidthPixels, RIGHT_MARGIN_PIXELS and the rowTexts/rowColors/rowActions/lineTexts/lineRows/rowFirstLines arrays are gone. Its rows are one HyperString with wrapping on (clearRows makes it, addRow appends one line per row with the row's colour and click on every word). layout(camera) sets the view to the box and calls HyperString.setLineOffsetFromTopRow to wrap and count the rows used (rowsUsed). The per-line overload gives the centred row's first row and the rows it takes; the scroll limit, centring and the controls box height use those counts. draw is Font.drawHyperStringRows at a whole-row offset. HyperString changes (shared with InfoPane, Terminal, ShaderCodePane, tool info panes and tooltips): (1) when wrap is on, the multi-line setLineOffsetFromTopRow first splits any static word wider than the view into pieces that fit, keeping its colour and actions (a hard break for an unbroken token); (2) a wrap never fires on the first word of a row (offset 0), so a too-wide first word no longer leaves a blank row before it. Both only change lines with a single word wider than the view or longer than charWrap; other wrapped text lays out as before. Font is unchanged. Pre-existing and left alone: HyperWord hit-tests with the raw, unscaled font width, so a word's click area runs far past its drawn width. In the menu every word of a row has the same action, and a click on a wrapped row loads it once (one 'loading' log line).

Rework 4 h (2026-10-03): MeshNodeViewerScene imports neither java.nio.file nor java.io.File (java.io.IOException only), and its Path/Files code, requestedModel, dslResourceFile, workingCopyOf and the DSL_RESOURCE_DIRECTORY/DSL_BUILD_DIRECTORY constants are gone. ModelCatalog now owns repoDslRoot() (src/main/resources/dsl, else under the module directory), trackedDslFile(name), packagedGraph(name) (a DSL choice: the tracked file plus the packaged resource name), launchChoice(token, catalog) (-Dixdar.model: a directory is a collection, then a catalog token, then a .dsl or mesh path, tried under the module directory) and indexOfFile. ModelChoice gained resourceName, workingFile() (where a reload reads and a save writes: build-output graphs map to their src/main/resources copy), readSource() (UTF-8), loadPackagedSource() (the web path) and openCollection(). ModelScene.openCollection takes the ModelChoice. workingDslPath() keeps its contract (the last-read file, else the launched graph's tracked file) and now asks the choice.

Rework 4 verification: MenuScrollBoxWrapTest rewritten over HyperString. It loads the real font atlas over a no-op GL proxy, because the unit suite has no GL context. Its 5 tests cover: rows that fit take one row; a long row wraps, every wrapped row's words click that row and not the next; an unbroken token is cut into pieces that fit with no blank row before it; scroll limit and centring count HyperString's rows; whole-row draw offsets. ScrollRegionHitTest is unaffected (4/4). ModelCatalogTest gained launch-property resolution and the tracked-copy read/save target (5/5). mvn test: 359 run, 0 failures. mvn -q compile: checkstyle-clean. tools/teavm-build.sh: OK, 0 errors. ixd wt done: passed. ring-tool (fertility_rings.dsl): on open the current graph is centred in the models box (tmp/view12-r4-menu-opened.png). Wheel at x 606/800/1020 over each box scrolls that box only, and the orbit stays az 0.7854 el 0.4189 d 268.5152; over the mesh it zooms (tmp/r4-probe.txt). With IXDAR_MODEL_DIR=tmp/staging-wrap, the staged 70-character name wraps onto three rows inside the box, its unbroken token hard-broken (tmp/view12-r4-wrapped-model-row.png). A click on its last row loaded it once and highlighted all three rows (tmp/view12-r4-wrapped-model-row-clicked.png). Item h: launch -Dixdar.mesh.dsl=fixtures/view12_rings_copy.dsl (a throwaway copy) put the cursor on it [24/39]; R, click, Enter, Ctrl+S logged 'saved 1 ring(s) to src/main/resources/dsl/fixtures/view12_rings_copy.dsl'. After switching to skull and back through the catalog, a second save went to the same file by absolute path. The copy was deleted, and the sha256 of fertility_rings.dsl is unchanged. -Dixdar.model=<dir of 2 meshes> opened a collection (2 members, manifest written, a_hand loaded); -Dixdar.model=skull resolved through the catalog.
